subject: blue jeans
title: What If You Never Washed Your Jeans?

scenes.text: What if you never washed your jeans? One student tried it for 15 months. The bacteria surprised everyone.
He wore the same raw denim well over 200 times, airing them out three times a week.
By month seven they smelled so bad he put them in the freezer. They came out odourless.
After 15 months, a scientist swabbed them: up to 10,000 bacteria colonies per square centimetre in the crotch.
Then he washed them, wore them just 13 days, and tested again. The count was about the same.
No E. coli, nothing dangerous, just bacteria from his own skin. Two weeks or 15 months, your jeans end up the same.

description:
What if you never washed your jeans? A University of Alberta student wore the same raw denim for 15 months and over 200 days without washing it.
A textile scientist found 8,000 to 10,000 bacterial colonies per square centimetre in the crotch, all normal skin bacteria, with no E. coli. After he washed them and wore them 13 more days, the counts were about the same. He froze them once in month seven to kill the smell.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: The textile scientist still recommended washing them about once a month, mostly for the smell. How long do your jeans go between washes?
